description_short: Aggregate metals ALE Table 2 by direction (anisotropic vs. isotropic) to compute the number of distinct metals and mean EPC per direction.

paper.title: Anisotropic/Isotropic Atomic Layer Etching of Metals

tables_modeled.label: Table 2
tables_modeled.description: Summary of anisotropic and isotropic metal ALE chemistries, including direction, modification/removal chemistry, EPC, process temperature, and cycle time.

comparisons.table_source: Table 2 (metals ALE processes) from the metal ALE review.

properties_used.label: Direction
properties_used.role: Specifies whether the ALE process is anisotropic or isotropic; used as the grouping key.

properties_used.label: Material
properties_used.role: Identifies the metal being etched; normalized to count distinct metals per direction.

properties_used.label: EPC (Å/cycle)
properties_used.role: Etch-per-cycle rate, parsed as a numeric value and averaged per direction group.

aggregation.description: Rows are grouped by etch direction (anisotropic vs. isotropic). Within each group, distinct metals are counted and EPC values are averaged.

output_shape.description: One row per etch direction (anisotropic / isotropic).
columns: n_metals: number of distinct metal materials with at least one reported process for this direction.
avg_epc: average etch-per-cycle rate (Å/cycle) over all processes in this direction.

postprocessing_notes.interpretation: The result summarizes directional trends in metal ALE. Comparing avg_epc and n_metals between anisotropic and isotropic regimes highlights which direction tends to achieve higher average etch rates and how broadly each regime has been explored across different metals.
